## A1: No definition of AI, though section B says AI is embedded in everyday tools

**Verdict: confirmed.** The draft holds no Definition at either layer (no "means", no "defined"). Section B states that AI is "increasingly embedded in tools", and C.2 (approved purposes only) and C.6 (vetting before adoption) speak of AI and AI tools with no scope, so whether the existing tool stack's embedded features are inside C.2 and C.6 is not decidable from the text.

**What the corpus changes:** Three definitions the draft could have adopted are in the corpus. The Act (Educ. 7-2201) defines AI by reference to State Finance and Procurement 3.5-801, whose "machine-based system" text the SB 720 fiscal note quotes (3.5-801 itself is not in the corpus). MSDE's K-12 guidance defines AI and states its scope covers every tool "regardless of how they are accessed". The MSDE model policy, which the draft adapts (N2), defines AI and Generative AI. MSDE's Local Policy Considerations asks the exact question the draft leaves open ("embedded AI features within existing platforms"). DI-RA already defines Technology to include software systems and online resources.

## A2: "Approved" has no approver, criteria or list; the Act contemplates a coordinator and approved tools

**Verdict: confirmed.** C.2's restriction to "approved" purposes names no approver, and C.6's vetting names no party (the extractor marked both with no responsible party stated). The draft contains no "coordinator" at either layer, while the Act requires each local system to designate one and to use MSDE's rubric in selecting AI tools.

**What the corpus changes:** AACPS already has approval routes the draft does not name: DL-RA sends instructional digital resources holding PII through Policy IH and Regulation IH-RA, and non-instructional ones to the Chief Information Officer; DI-RA requires CIO approval of free and open-source software. IH and IH-RA are not Related Entries of the draft (N3). The model policy assigns the procedure to the Superintendent ("procedures for vetting and approving"); the draft dropped it.

## A3: C.1's "consequential decision" and "documented human oversight" are undefined

**What the corpus changes:** The MSDE model policy, whose C.1 sentence the draft copies word for word, defines both "Consequential Use" and "Human Oversight"; the draft kept the sentence and dropped the definitions. ## A4: C.1 gives "employees and stakeholders" authority to override AI outputs; B counts students as stakeholders

**Verdict: confirmed.** C.1 grants the authority to "interpret, contextualize, override, or reject AI outputs" to employees and stakeholders, and section B lists students among the stakeholders. Read together, a student holds authority to override an AI output in a consequential decision about a student.

**What the corpus changes:** The words "and stakeholders" are the draft's own: the MSDE model policy gives the authority to employees only, and its definition of Human Oversight confines it to "a qualified employee".

## A5: C.7 says "when opt-out options apply" but creates no opt-out; PPRA gives one; silent on COPPA school consent

**Verdict: partial.** Confirmed that C.7 is a duty to communicate, not a right: it is the draft's only mention of opting out, and no draft statement grants one. PPRA (cited in the draft's Legal References) requires local policies that let a parent opt a student out of the activities it lists. The COPPA leg does not hold as stated: the COPPA rule in the corpus (16 CFR 312, 45,303 characters) never mentions schools, so school consent on a parent's behalf is not in the corpus's text at all (it is FTC guidance, not held); the draft's silence matches the rule it cites.

**What the corpus changes:** The draft's C.7 is MSDE's sentence nearly verbatim (K-12 guidance and model policy alike), so the gap is inherited, not introduced.

## A6: C.3 bias monitoring needs protected-class outcome data, in tension with data minimization; no direction

**Verdict: partial.** C.3 obliges AACPS to monitor for biased or discriminatory outcomes and gives no direction on the data that takes. But the tension DN-002 names is not in the draft: the draft has no data-minimization duty at either layer. It is between C.3 and MSDE's expectation that districts "minimize data collection", which the draft does not carry.

**What the corpus changes:** MSDE's guidance supplies the direction the anchor asks for: equity monitoring "within existing equity review structures". The model policy also pairs monitoring with evaluation for bias before adoption, which the draft dropped.

## A7: B names academic integrity and over-reliance as risks; C addresses neither; student use deferred to C.4

**Verdict: confirmed.** Section B names both risks; no draft Obligation mentions integrity or reliance. C.4 defers student use to expectations AACPS "shall establish", and C.5's professional learning omits both.

**What the corpus changes:** The Act requires the professional development it funds to cover "academic integrity, and means of avoiding overdependence", which C.5 does not list. The model policy carries the integrity rules the draft dropped: expectations for when unaided work is required, and no reliance on AI detection tools (MSDE's guidance likewise).

## A8: Drafting: "biased, discrimination, or inequitable"; "never replace" vs "may not replace"; no review clause

**Verdict: confirmed.** All three hold. C.3 reads "biased, discrimination, or inequitable" (the model has "biased or inequitable"). B says AI shall "never replace" professional judgment and C.1 that it "may not replace" professional expertise. The draft contains no "review" at either layer.

**What the corpus changes:** The Act requires MSDE to review its guidance every year, and the policy must be "aligned with the guidance", so an unreviewed policy drifts out of alignment by statute. MSDE asks districts to "review and revise policies annually"; the model policy has the Superintendent "periodically review" the regulations.

## N2 (new): The draft is the MSDE model policy with its definitions and most of its safeguards removed

**Verdict: confirmed.** Clause by clause (the table below), the draft's Obligations are the model's, reworded ("AACPS" for "[NCPS]", "AI" for "artificial intelligence"). What did not carry over is listed under the table: the model's seven Definitions, its prohibited uses (PII into unapproved tools, final consequential decisions without human review, biometric collection), data minimization, academic-integrity and detection-tool rules, AI literacy instruction, the operational higher-risk rule, vendor contract terms, the cross-functional team, the Superintendent's procedures and periodic reporting to the Board. None is present in the draft at either layer. Where a clause did carry over it is sometimes thinned: C.4 keeps one general sentence ("expectations, conditions, and limitations for student use") in place of the model's expectations for when AI use is permitted, when unaided work is required and how AI assistance is acknowledged.

## N3 (new): The draft's Related Entries omit IH and IH-RA, the existing approval path for instructional digital tools

**Verdict: confirmed.** DL-RA routes instructional digital resources that hold PII through Policy IH and Regulation IH-RA (materials of instruction) and lists IH and IH-RA among its own Related Entries. The draft lists DL and DL-RA but not IH or IH-RA, so the one existing route by which an instructional AI tool is "approved" (A2) is not connected to C.2. IH and IH-RA are not in this corpus; a comment citing them should be checked against their published text.
